verdict.rationale: Greptile's security page documents its own retention-related control: customers can turn off logging to make chats private. In self-hosted deployments, logs stay only on customer servers, so customers control where retained data lives. There is no documented retention period, deletion request, or purge mechanism, and the vendor reserves the right to keep de-identified customer data for analytics and AI training. Missing for 10: configurable retention windows, documented data deletion/purge controls, an opt-out from de-identified AI-training use, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can control data retention and deletion

citations.quote: Customers can choose to turn off logging and make chats 100% private. Note that in the self-hosted service, logs are stored on customer servers only.
Deploy Greptile in your own infrastructure with Docker Compose. Supports AWS, GCP, Azure, air-gapped environments, and custom LLM configurations.
